---
name: verify
description: Compare selected Exposed searches and authoritative MP and organisation totals with live production, using an isolated snapshot-backed Compose build of the current worktree. Use after search, grouping, totals, or public loader changes.
---

# Verify against live production

Read [the feature map](features/README.md). From the repository root:

```sh
npm ci --prefix .agents/skills/verify
npm test --prefix .agents/skills/verify
./.agents/skills/verify/scripts/run-snapshot-comparison.sh
```

For totals or ranking changes, also run the
[current-term checks](features/current-term-totals.md). Production parity alone
does not prove that totals exclude earlier and undated records. Report the
current-term result separately from the live comparison result.

Require Docker Compose, Node with built-in fetch/test, curl, and an existing
`exposed_search_regression` snapshot in container `exposed-postgres-1` (user
`exposed`). Override those prerequisite identities with `VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_CONTAINER`,
`VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_DATABASE`, and `VERIFY_SNAPSHOT_USER` when necessary. The helper
can start a stopped source container and restores that initial state; it never
stops a source container that was already running. Do not run during snapshot
refresh. A missing snapshot is a failed prerequisite, never permission to ingest.
The [refresh helper](scripts/refresh-search-regression-db.sh) remains a separate,
deliberate replacement operation requiring its documented source-client shutdown.

The helper creates a unique project for this worktree/run, dumps one consistent
source snapshot, builds this worktree's backend/frontend with the production
Dockerfiles, and restores into its own PostgreSQL volume. Only that disposable
copy receives current migrations; checksum mismatches fail without alignment.
It does not rerun ingestion or refresh stored groups. The backend uses a read-only
connection; the frontend reaches its private API within the project's network.
No shared target/cache volumes or database ports are mounted. A random loopback
frontend port supplies the comparator's development origin. Doctor checks backend
health and decodes a successful public search model before comparison.

Production defaults to `https://exposed.today`. Every invocation reads it live
with bounded sequential GETs through the same SvelteKit page-data loaders used by
the public frontend. [The manifest](live-cases.json) contains selectors only,
never expected money. Resolve funder UUIDs independently in each environment by
one exact name/kind match, then assert the identity returned by each detail page.
Member Parliament IDs and names must match. Missing or ambiguous identities,
error models, malformed fields, redirects, HTTP failures and timeouts fail closed.

Compare supplied decimal strings/null without arithmetic, rounding, currency
conversion, or fallback totals. Search preserves order, duplicate multiplicity,
match provenance and entity context. Totals include authoritative declared periods,
counts/completeness, currencies/categories, parties and ranked recipients. Arrays
retain the public loader's order. Installation-local funder UUIDs are omitted only
from semantic comparisons; raw responses retain them.

The printed new evidence directory survives success, mismatch, failure and cleanup.
It records the worktree commit/dirty status, source container and snapshot, unique
Compose project, derived origin, build/migration/doctor/container/cleanup logs,
raw request URLs/status/headers/body/timestamps, normalized observations, incremental
`http/report.json`, and readable `http/diff.txt`. An interrupted comparator leaves
an incomplete report and available partial evidence. Treat incomplete evidence as
failure. Evidence retains the database dump.

Exit 0 requires every observation to succeed and match. Exit 1 means observed field
differences; exit 2 means observation/configuration/schema/identity errors (which
take precedence over differences). Report the code and evidence paths. Snapshot
age or live production changes can explain discrepancies, but discrepancies still
fail; investigate provenance before attributing them to branch code. Never edit
expected totals or refresh data to manufacture parity. There is no baseline-update
mode. If the snapshot predates grouped funder metadata, missing group identities
can be valid observed errors.

Cleanup always removes only this run's Compose project and volumes, including on
failure. It retains the source snapshot and filesystem evidence. Check
`cleanup.log`; failed cleanup is exit 2. Do not use blanket Docker prune/down.

For controlled HTTP replay or diagnosis, the internal observer accepts explicit
origins; this alone does not prove a worktree build:

```sh
node .agents/skills/verify/scripts/compare-live.mjs --development http://127.0.0.1:PORT
```

Optional `--production ORIGIN`, `--cases PATH`, and `--evidence NEW_DIRECTORY` select
a controlled reference, selector subset, or evidence location. Equal origins are
rejected. The lifecycle command accepts only `--production` and `--cases`; it always
derives its own development origin and evidence directory. No production writes,
CI changes or financial-semantic changes are part of verification.
# Build and run the production image

Build from the repository root with Docker Buildx:

```sh
docker buildx build --load -f docker/Dockerfile -t exposed:local .
docker run --rm exposed:local --help
```

The build requires no database connection. It uses committed SQLx query metadata,
Rust 1.98.1, and cargo-chef 0.1.78. Dependency compilation uses ordinary Docker
layers so the CI GitHub Actions cache includes compiled dependencies. The default
build parallelism is two jobs. Set `--build-arg CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4` to change it.

The `binary`, `migrate`, and `data` targets share the release binary and Debian
runtime in `docker/Dockerfile`. Its default target is `binary`, which runs
`exposed server` on port 6999 as UID and GID 10001. Build the other backend targets
with `--target migrate` or `--target data`. The independent
`docker/Dockerfile.frontend` contains Node and the SvelteKit build. Its default
target is `frontend-server`. Use distinct local tags for each target.

```sh
docker buildx build --load -f docker/Dockerfile --target migrate -t exposed:migrate .
docker buildx build --load -f docker/Dockerfile.frontend --target frontend-server -t exposed:frontend-server .
docker buildx build --load -f docker/Dockerfile --target data -t exposed:data .
export DATABASE_URL='REDACTED'
docker run --rm --env DATABASE_URL exposed:migrate
docker run --rm --env EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN=http://backend:6999 -p 8080:8080 exposed:frontend-server
docker run --rm --env DATABASE_URL -p 6999:6999 exposed:local
```

The search queries qualify `pg_trgm` functions and operators with the `exposed`
schema, so the connection does not need a custom search path.

The migration image runs `exposed migrate run --source /app/db/migrations` and
contains the versioned SQL assets. Run it explicitly before starting the Rust
server. See [database migrations](../db/README.md) for existing database upgrades.

The frontend image runs the locked SvelteKit build directly through Node on port
8080 as UID and GID 10001. It contains no Rust binary and needs no `DATABASE_URL`.
Deploy the Rust server separately and set the frontend's private
`EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN` environment variable to the backend's reachable origin, such
as `http://backend:6999`. The example above requires `backend` to resolve on a
container network shared by both deployments. Server page loaders call this
origin; browser navigation uses SvelteKit page data. The backend does not need a
public route or an `/api/` ingress rule.

The data image runs `exposed data --help` by default. Pass a data subcommand
directly, including `util` commands. Mount configuration and writable data
directories for ingestion.

```sh
docker run --rm --mount type=bind,src="$PWD/config.yaml",dst=/config.yaml,readonly \
    --mount type=bind,src="$PWD/data",dst=/data \
    exposed:data util latest --config /config.yaml
```

Use `data_dir: /data` in the mounted configuration and give UID 10001 access to
the mounted data directory. Pass `--env DATABASE_URL` for data commands that
access PostgreSQL.

## Run on macOS

Automatic releases support `linux/amd64`, including Docker Desktop on Intel
Macs. On Apple Silicon, use the manual ARM test workflow described below or build
locally. Local builds use the Docker builder's default platform.

The containers run inside Docker Desktop's Linux VM. Use the matching immutable
references with the `docker run` commands above. You do not need `--platform` for
native images. Historical multi-platform digest references remain valid and
Docker still selects their matching architecture.

If PostgreSQL runs on your Mac, use `host.docker.internal` as the host in
`DATABASE_URL`. PostgreSQL must accept connections from Docker Desktop.

## Refresh SQLx query metadata

Use an isolated PostgreSQL 18 database. Set `DATABASE_URL` to that database, then
run these commands from the repository root:

```sh
cargo install sqlx-cli --version 0.9.0 --locked --no-default-features --features postgres,rustls,sqlx-toml
sqlx migrate run --config sqlx.toml --source db/migrations
cargo sqlx prepare --workspace -- --bin exposed
cargo sqlx prepare --check --workspace -- --bin exposed
```

Commit the resulting `.sqlx` files with query or migration changes. The image
build uses this metadata offline. Refresh and check it against PostgreSQL manually
when queries or migrations change.
No database URL or credentials enter the Docker build.

## Releases from main

The release workflow publishes on pushes to `main` that change Rust, frontend,
migrations, SQLx metadata, Docker, or release inputs, including the shared
`.github/actions/build-images` action. It builds all four variants on a native
`ubuntu-24.04` runner for `linux/amd64`. CI uses Docker, `gh`, and `jq`, without
host Rust or SQLx installations.

### Source

Read-only Git history and GitHub PR archaeology in `johnnylarner/exposed`.

### Direct evidence

- [PR #103](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/103), merged October 22, explicitly documents a prior defect: “A presentation change narrowed member headlines to employment and silently changed their totals.” It restores all-category declared GBP totals and backend ownership. Its recorded Farage total is **£2,323,720.45** for both historical and current-term headlines.
- [PR #50](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/50) independently records “The live Nigel Farage total is £2,323,720.45.” Its weekly chart groups by **registration week because payment dates are unavailable**.
- [PR #126](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/126) warns: “Production parity can pass when both environments include records from before this parliamentary term.” This PR changes verification documentation only; it does not establish a production bug.
- [PR #115](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/115) explicitly preserves existing term/history totals while adding UTC calendar-year totals. All categories participate; known foreign currencies are excluded without conversion; missing GBP amounts and unknown currencies mark incompleteness.
- [PR #125](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/125) states MP rankings use **all categories**, registrations on or after **9 July 2024**, and exact GBP amounts.
- [PR #22](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/22) describes preserving individual source funding occurrences and reports independent checking of every occurrence in a 655-partition capture.
- [PR #39](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/39) explicitly says source-ID migration preserves “empty partitions and repeated occurrences.”
- [PR #62](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/62) adds correction-aware daily synchronization. **Automatic declaration retirement remains outside its scope.**

### Code/history evidence

- `git blame` places current `DeclaredTotalsAggregate` predominantly in #118 (`4d3d7e0`); the all-category authority derives from #103 (`b27fa96`). #125 (`637cee8`) moves shared aggregation into `domain/models/declared_totals.rs`.
- `PeriodAggregate::observe` sums each stored entry’s amount exactly once. There is no repeated-payment expansion at this stage.
- `outbound/declaration_source.rs` history is #17 → #22 → #23. Its `FundingFields` reads `Value` and `PaymentType`, but no recurrence count, payment dates or frequency. `funding_entries` preserves anchored nested occurrences. **This establishes mechanics, not an identified repeated-payment defect.**
- Production defaults to **https://exposed.today** in `.agents/skills/verify/SKILL.md:41` and `scripts/compare-live.mjs:236`.

### Searches and coverage

Executed:

- `git blame -L 59,139 exposed/src/lib/domain/services/entity_details.rs`
- `git log --follow` on `declared_totals.rs` and `declaration_source.rs`
- `git log --all --grep='payment\|totals\|extract' -i`
- `git log --all --grep='repeat\|parser\|payment\|parse\|amount' -i`
- `git log --all --grep='clean\|dedup\|repeat' -i`
- Reviewed full PR bodies/comments/reviews for **#125, #115, #103, #47, #22, #62, #39, #126, #17, #11**.
- Listed all 129 PR titles; searched PR bodies with `extract OR payment OR amount OR parser`.
- Read parser implementation and #103/#125 patches.

Opened PRs mostly have no comments or reviews. #17’s sole substantive inline comment concerns README content and is unrelated.

### Gaps

No explicit historical discussion explaining a discrepancy with OpenInterests, or documenting a known recurring-payment parser defect, surfaced. Historical Farage **£2,323,720.45** is a recorded observation, not proof of today’s production total. Data freshness, corrected/retired declarations, recurring payment interpretation, and differing category scope still require live record reconciliation.

The Register of Members' Financial Interests contains information about any financial interest an MP has, or any benefit they receive, which someone else might reasonably consider to influence what they say or do as an MP.

MPs must register any change to their registrable interests within 28 days.

Interests remain on the Register for twelve months after they have expired.

REGISTER OF MEMBERS' FINANCIAL INTERESTS 
Updates 3 – 30 September 2024 
 
 
The Register is maintained by the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards. 
 
It is updated fortnightly online when Parliament is sitting, and less frequently at other times. 
 
MPs must register all their current financial interests, and any registrable benefits (other than 
earnings) received in the 12 months before their election within one month of their election, 
and MPs must register any change in those registrable interests within 28 days. 
 
Interests remain on the Register for 12 months after their date of registration, most recent 
update or end date, whichever is later. 
 
This document contains only those interests added since the previous version of the Register. 
 
Entries in bold italics indicates interests that have been subject to an investigation by the 
Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards and subsequently rectified. 
 
Rectification decisions, together with the relevant evidence, are published on the 
Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards’ section of the Parliament website.  
 
For appointments registered under ‘Category 1: Employment and earnings’, MPs who ceased 
to hold Ministerial office within the previous two years are required to state whether they 
sought the advice of the Advisory Committee on Business Appointments (ACOBA). 
 
This document does not include minor corrections.

The House created a system of registration of interests as a key way of delivering the Nolan principle of openness, which, along with the other Principles of Public Life, the Code of Conduct requires Members to uphold. Under Standing Order No. 150(2)(a), my principal duties as Commissioner include:

“to maintain the Register of Members’ Financial Interests and any other registers of interest established by the House, and to make such arrangements for the compilation, maintenance and accessibility of those registers as are approved by the Committee on Standards or an appropriate sub-committee thereof”.

Register of Members’ Financial Interests

43. The main purpose of the Register of Members’ Financial Interests (RMFI) is to provide information about any financial interest which a Member has, or any benefit which he or she receives, which others might reasonably consider to influence his or her actions or words as a Member of Parliament (see paragraph 5 of the Introduction to the Guide to the Rules).

44. I am responsible for preparing the RMFI, which is updated online (every two weeks when the House is sitting, and less frequently at other times) under the authority of the House of Commons Committee on Standards. Entries remain in the Register for 12 months after they have expired.34

As my last Annual Report described, the Committee on Standards recommended the development of a publicly available, downloadable, fully searchable form of the registers, to make it easier for the public to interrogate the data. ### Register of Members’ Financial Interests

From 00:01 on the day of dissolution there are no Members of Parliament (MPs) until after the General Election. The Registers do not operate during the dissolution period and the registration portal will also be closed during that time.

After the General Election, new Members must register all their current financial interests, and any registrable benefits (other than earnings) received in the 12 months before their election within one month of their election in the Register of Members’ Financial Interests (RMFI).

Members who are returned (that is, re-elected) must review their most recent entry in the RMFI (in the last Parliament) and submit any change to their registrable interests within one month of their election.

Thereafter, all Members must register any change to their registrable interests within 28 days.   

The Office of the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards will contact all Members to tell them how to register, to remind them of this deadline, and to offer support to help them fulfil their responsibilities under the Code of Conduct.

During the dissolution period, OPCS’s Registry Office cannot accept information relating to registrations, or information on donations received during the dissolution period – this information will need to be resubmitted to the Registry Office after the General Election.

Employment and earnings requirements has been simplified to: “Over £300 for the total of payments of whatever size from the same source in a calendar year”. (The “over £100” threshold has been removed)

5.8 The Register of Members' Financial Interests is compiled on the basis of the returns made by Members. The task of collating the returns is carried out under the authority of the Commissioner. It is the Commissioner's duty to send out the appropriate form for Members to complete at the beginning of each Parliament; a form is similarly sent to every Member returned at a by-election. It is the responsibility of Members to return the completed form within one month of their election to the House;1 it is also their responsibility to notify any changes in their registrable interests within four weeks of the changes occurring.

The Register is published, and regularly updated, on the parliamentary website. Entries which relate to single benefits or to interests which are no longer held remain in the Register for twelve months after such interests are received or relinquished.

The rules on the registration of financial interests are set out in the Guide to the Rules relating to the Conduct of Members. The registration form specifies categories of registrable interests, including remunerated company directorships or other employment, financial sponsorship, gifts or other benefits above a specified value, shareholdings, land and property. In some cases, these categories include financial interests of a spouse or partner. Members are also required to register family members employed and paid through parliamentary allowances.2

Register of interests and potential conflicts

**3. Process for identifying conflicts of interests**

**3.1.** On appointment, Committee members are required to declare any interests they have which might result in conflicts or be perceived to create conflicts in any area of the Committee’s work. Members are provided detailed guidance on managing conflicts of interest, based on Cabinet Office guidelines.

**3.2.** A Register of Interests (ROI) is maintained by the RPC secretariat and published on the website. The ROI is circulated to the Committee ahead of each formal Committee meeting (currently every two months) and a standing item on the agenda prompts members to review their interests and update the ROI as necessary. The ROI is updated immediately on notification of any changes and following each Committee meeting.

**3.3.** A conflict of interest is generally considered to be ‘time-expired’, 12 months after the committee member’s last connection with the third-party concerned. However, this will be considered on its own merit in each individual circumstance.

# MPs' register of interests

All financial interests which might be reasonably regarded as influencing the actions, words or votes of MPs must be registered.

21 MAY 2024

Beatrice Barr Finn Baker

4 min read This explainer was originally published on 8 November 2022.

Image: MPs sitting in the House of Commons

MPs must register their interests within 28 days of a new parliament beginning. Newly elected MPs must include any relevant interests (other than earnings) from the year prior to their election.

### What interests do MPs have to register?

The register of members’ financial interests records all financial interests which might be reasonably regarded as influencing the actions, words or votes of MPs. These interests are grouped into 10 categories, including outside earnings, donations and shareholdings.

The register has existed since 1974 and was made more rigorous in 1996 following recommendations from the new Committee on Standards in Public Life (CSPL). ^{undefined} BBC News, ‘Register of interests’, 24 October 2008, http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk_politics/a-z_of_parliament/r-s/82466.stm, retrieved 8 November 2022  The parliamentary commissioner for standards is responsible for maintaining the register, but MPs declare their interests through the office of the registrar, with details published on the parliamentary website.

### How often must MPs disclose their interests?

MPs must register their interests within 28 days of a new parliament beginning. Newly elected MPs must include any relevant interests (other than earnings) from the year prior to their election.

Any changes or additions after this initial period must also be registered within 28 days. Updates to the register are usually published fortnightly when the Commons is sitting, and less frequently during recess.

In addition to registering, MPs must declare any relevant interests at certain times, including when speaking in debates, when tabling written questions or motions, or when applying for urgent questions, emergency debates or an adjournment debate. ^{34} House of Commons, Guide to the Rules relating to the Conduct of Members, 10 February 2023, HC 1083, chapter 2  The category of interests that must be declared is wider than those that must be registered and includes expected future interests, the interests of family members and financial interests that fall below the financial thresholds. 

### What happens if MPs fail to disclose their interests?

The parliamentary commissioner for standards investigates alleged non-compliance by MPs. In most cases where a breach is found, the case is closed through the rectification process rather than through a referral to the Committee on Standards. This usually involves the MP making an apology and correcting the register. In some instances, MPs are referred for remedial training on the requirement to register.

The parliamentary commissioner for standards warned MPs that “a significant proportion of Members are habitually registering outside the 28-day time limits”. ^{35} Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards, ‘Late Registration of Interests’, Advice note, 3 February 2023, PCS/AN/2023.03

Former prime minister Boris Johnson was referred to the Committee on Standards in 2018 and 2019 for failing to register his interests on time. ^{36} House of Commons Committee on Standards, Boris Johnson, 6 December 2018, HC 1797; House of Commons Committee on Standards, Boris Johnson: Further Report, 8 April 2019, HC 2113  He was required to make an apology to the Commons on the first occasion and to attend training with the Registrar on the second. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

⁴⁸ Nevertheless, the primary emphasis in the regime is the careful consideration of MPs’ financial interests.

The Guide to the Rules provides detail on the Registration of Members Financial Interests.⁴⁹ MPs are required to register financial and other registrable benefits received in the previous 12 months before their election, within one month of entering parliament; and thereafter to register any benefits within 28 days (paragraph 2). Any MP who has a registrable interest must inform the Commissioner before undertaking “any action, speech or proceeding of the House” (paragraph 3).

The Guide to the Rules provides details of the requirements for registration. These include registering employment and earnings, donations and other support for activities as members of parliament, gifts, benefits and hospitality (UK and overseas), visits abroad, land and property, shareholdings, miscellaneous, employment of family members and family members engaged in lobbying. MPs can also get confidential advice on the requirements of registration from the Registrar of Members interests.

Parliament’s published rule keeps an interest on the register for **12 months after its registration, most recent update, or end date—whichever is later**.
